title: Uniform Ext bound
statement:
Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$. For every $C\in\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ there is an integer $d_C\geq0$ such that

$$
\Ext^q_{\Lambda}(C,N)=0
\qquad\text{for all }q>d_C\text{ and all }N\in\Cons(X,\Lambda),
$$

the Ext groups being taken in $\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$.

For $C=a_!L$, with $a$ factored as $S\hookrightarrow Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $j$ the open complement of
$Z$, the proof gives $d_C=\operatorname{cd}_\ell(j)+\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)+2$ (cohomological
dimensions as in [sk-def-cd]). One of the two extra degrees comes from the cone defining
$R\underline\Gamma_Z$, the other from a derived inverse limit over the reductions modulo $\pi_E^n$.

proof.text: Use the global finite-field datum and the coefficient-stage list of [sk-def-sf-setting], with $X$ separated and of finite type over that finite field or its algebraic closure. Only these standing data are used here; the finite-stage étale conventions in that definition are not an identification of the rational pro-étale coefficient categories. This is a standing scheme in the precise sense of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], since the field has characteristic $p\ne\ell$. For a locally closed $a=i\circ u:S\hookrightarrow Z\hookrightarrow X$, with $i$ closed and $u$ open, let $j:X\setminus Z\hookrightarrow X$ and put $c_a=\operatorname{cd}_\ell(j)+\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)+2$. The base field has finite $\ell$-cohomological dimension by [sk-lem-base-field-cd]. Finiteness for $S$ and $j$ follows from the finite-type bound in [sk-def-cd] (Stacks Tag 0F10). Thus $\max(0,c_a)$ is a finite nonnegative integer. Empty strata can be omitted.

source.place: opening paragraph: finiteness of the two cohomological dimensions

proof.text: Fix such an $a$ and a lisse $\Lambda_S$-module $L$. Apply [det-uniform-constructible-ext-rational] with these $a,L$ and an arbitrary locally closed $b:T\hookrightarrow X$ and lisse $\Lambda_T$-module $M$. Its displayed conclusion is $\Ext^q_\Lambda(a_!L,b_!M)=0$ for $q>c_a$, for both $\Lambda=E$ and $\Qlb$. Use the uniform assertion in that statement: $c_a$ does not depend on $b$ or $M$. The finite stratifications in that lemma are the preparation for its stratum calculation; the formula there is written for these $a_!L,b_!M$. In particular this use does not assume a global integral lattice in an arbitrary lisse rational sheaf. The integral inputs identify the two extra degrees in the stated estimate: [det-uniform-constructible-ext-torsion](2) has cutoff $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(j)+\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)+1$, and [det-uniform-constructible-ext-integral] has cutoff $c_a$. Here $X$ is a standing scheme by Step 1, $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$ is admissible, and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ is closed with open complement $j$, so the hypotheses of [sk-lem-formal-closed-support] hold. Its support fiber formula in part (1) and the limit compatibility in [sk-lem-formal-closed-support-ii] are the support and inverse-limit constructions occurring in this calculation; the torsion and integral estimates are taken from their statements, not reconstructed from unstated completeness assertions.

source.place: Lattices; Torsion targets; Integral targets; Inverting pi_E; The case Lambda=Qlb (the existing rational stratum lemma packages the last two passages)

proof.text: Keep $a,L$ fixed and let $N$ be any constructible target. By [sk-lem-coefficient-heart](1,3), choose a finite filtration $0=N_0\subset\cdots\subset N_r=N$ by sheaves, with $G_t=N_t/N_{t-1}=b_{t,!}M_t$ and all inclusions and quotient maps exact in the ambient module category. Induct on $t$ on the assertion that $\Ext^q_\Lambda(a_!L,N_t)=0$ for every $q>\max(0,c_a)$. For $t=0$ this is additivity of Ext, as defined in [def-pc-ext]. At the induction step [lem-sc-abelian-ext-covariant-exact], in the abelian category of all $\Lambda_X$-module sheaves, gives the exact segment $\Ext^q(a_!L,N_{t-1})\to\Ext^q(a_!L,N_t)\to\Ext^q(a_!L,G_t)$. Both end groups vanish, the first by induction and the second by Step 2, so the middle group is zero. Thus the same bound works for all $N$, independently of the length and strata of its filtration. These are Ext groups in the ambient derived category, by [def-pc-ext], not Ext groups formed in the constructible heart.

source.place: opening paragraph: finite filtration of the target and its common bound

proof.text: Now take $C\in\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ and fix once and for all a filtration $0=C_0\subset\cdots\subset C_m=C$ from [sk-lem-coefficient-heart](3), with $C_s/C_{s-1}=a_{s,!}L_s$. Set $d_C=\max(\{0\}\cup\{\max(0,c_{a_s}):1\le s\le m\})$. This is finite by Step 1, depends on the chosen filtration of $C$ alone, and is nonnegative. For every constructible $N$ and $q>d_C$, induct on $s$. The base $C_0=0$ has zero Ext by additivity [def-pc-ext]. For the short exact sequence $0\to C_{s-1}\to C_s\to a_{s,!}L_s\to0$, [lem-coef-ext-contravariant-six-term] gives $\Ext^q(a_{s,!}L_s,N)\to\Ext^q(C_s,N)\to\Ext^q(C_{s-1},N)$. Step 3 and the induction hypothesis kill the end groups, hence $\Ext^q(C_s,N)=0$. At $s=m$ this proves the claim, simultaneously for every $N$. For $C=0$ the empty filtration gives $d_C=0$. If $C=a_!L$, omit this last source filtration and apply Step 3 directly: its cutoff is the stated $c_a$ (with a nonnegative bound chosen if the source is zero).

source.place: opening paragraph: finite filtration of the source, maximum of the finitely many bounds; statement: the single-stratum bound
